candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide education about health promotion and disease prevention and reinforce modifiable lifestyle risk-factor interventions.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — hypertension prevention through lifestyle modification
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with elevated blood pressure that DASH-style eating, sodium reduction, regular physical activity, and healthy weight management are evidence-based measures to prevent or treat hypertension.

options.A: Avoid physical activity until blood pressure returns to normal.
options.B: Follow a heart-healthy pattern such as DASH, reduce sodium, stay physically active, and work toward a healthy weight.
options.C: Lifestyle changes have little role unless antihypertensive medication has already been started.
options.D: Increase sodium intake when exercising so dietary changes do not affect blood pressure.

candidate.rationale: The 2025 ACC/AHA high blood pressure guideline strongly recommends lifestyle changes for prevention and treatment of elevated blood pressure and hypertension, including a heart-healthy eating pattern such as DASH, reduced sodium intake, regular physical activity, and maintaining or achieving a healthy weight. B directly reflects this guidance. A and C contradict the guideline's emphasis on lifestyle intervention, while D reverses the sodium recommendation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current hypertension guidance supports DASH-style eating, lower sodium intake, physical activity, and weight management as core lifestyle measures for elevated blood pressure and hypertension.
candidate.source_document_title: 2025 Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
candidate.source_locator: Top Things to Know, item 5: lifestyle changes are strongly recommended for all adults to prevent or treat elevated blood pressure/hypertension, including healthy weight, heart-healthy eating such as DASH, sodium reduction, moderate physical activity, stress management, and reducing/eliminating alcohol.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association (AHA) and American College of Cardiology (ACC)
candidate.stem: A client with elevated blood pressure asks which lifestyle changes can help prevent progression to hypertension. Which teaching is most consistent with the current guideline?
